title: indexing an Int ignores the index: k[1], k[-1] and k[n] read and write k with no error
reproducer:
def three() -> Int:
    return 3


def main():
    var k = 7
    print(k[1], k[-1], k[three()])
    k[1] = 5
    print(k)
compiler: accepts and prints `7 7 7`, then `5`, also with -O0 and -D ASSERT=all: SIMD.__getitem__ and __setitem__ (std/simd.mojo:1193 and 1209 at 10c54f6f5b) lower to pop.simd.extractelement and insertelement with no bounds check, and every index probed acts on the one element
fixed: checks the index of an Int as the index of an array of length 1, as `var k = [7]` is checked on the pin: a constant index out of range is rejected ("constraint failed: index is out of bounds", or "negative indexing is not supported" when negative), and a computed one fails at run time ("index 3 is out of bounds, valid range is 0 to 0")
model: rejects the reproducer as constantIndexOutOfBounds, for k[1]; with the constant indices removed, it fails at run time with indexOutOfBounds at k[three()]

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular; its evidence is an analogy with arrays, which neither the docs nor the compiler states for Int

nightly.result: accepts and prints `7 7 7`, then `5`; with `var k = [7]` the constant indices are rejected and k[three()] fails at run time
